balloons.head: Character window
balloons.text: Everything about you: what you carry and wear, health, temperature, ID, journal and skills.
The world around you: containers, crafting, building, furniture, maps, foraging, animals and vehicles.
balloons.head: World window

balloons.text: The belt: your off hand and main hand at the left end, then the numbered slots on a strap. The green ring shows the main hand's condition.

shots.title: Old job
shots.caption: Angel pumped gas at the Fossoil. Six days in, Mechanics is at 7 and Welding at 6; Cooking is still 2.

balloons.text: Mechanics at 7, with a +125% XP boost.
Welding at 6, with +75% XP.
Cooking is still at 2.
A mechanic, six days in, 23 zombies killed.
Hair and beard: Now is your look, After previews a pick.
Good traits carry a green mark.
Bad ones carry a red mark.

shots.title: The plan
shots.caption: A flyer for the old station, and a note in the journal.

balloons.text: One page for the journal, notebooks, papers and recipes.
Type an entry and press Save to add it to the log.
Each entry carries the day and time it was written.
Paper shows the page; Words shows the text.
The places a flyer names. Show on map marks the place on the map.

shots.title: The route
shots.caption: World window, Maps tab.

balloons.text: Pick a mark up, then click the map to put it down. Aa writes a note.
The key shows what the colors on the Survey map mean.
Survey, Color or Paper picks the map style.
The red words are a note on the map.
A flyer you have read pins its place: a paper with a red thumbtack. The blue tick means you have been there.

shots.title: Driving in
shots.caption: Seat chooser and dashboard.

balloons.text: Seat 1, lit, is the driver's. The heading names the seat under the pointer.
The help line at the foot says what the pointer is on.
The fuel gauge. The needle is on E.
The dashboard is drawn to match the car. This is the station wagon's.

shots.title: Fixing the car
shots.caption: World window, Vehicle tab.

balloons.text: The part card: this tire is missing.
Parts you can fit, from your bags and nearby.
About says what the part does.
The Vehicle tab opens when you are next to a car.
Install fits the part picked below.
While the job runs, a band shows the part and the percent.
The action bar over the car: installing the tire, 35 percent.

shots.title: Barricading
shots.caption: Context menu on the front window, and the action bar.

balloons.text: The label names the action under the pointer: Window, Barricade (Planks).
The strip is a submenu: < goes back, the lit button is the one under the pointer.
The action bar shows the action, the step and the percent: step 2 of 3, 39 percent.

shots.title: Stocking shelves
shots.caption: Character window on the left, World window on the right, with three shelves and the ground.

balloons.text: The title bar counts the containers: 2 here, 4 on the right.
Each column header shows its weight and item count.
These buttons list the containers in reach: three shelves and the ground.
Drag an item from one column to another to move it. Here, a Diet Cola is dragged to the first shelf.
Each shelf in reach has its own column.
The ground is a column too. Nothing is on it here.

shots.title: Open for business
shots.caption: The Fossoil's colors, set from the window menu: Light theme, Blue accent.

balloons.head: Window menu
balloons.text: The box at the right end of the title bar pulls it down.

balloons.head: Theme
balloons.text: Dark, Light or High contrast. A check mark shows the one in use.

balloons.head: Accent
balloons.text: Nine colors for this window, or Same as Accent color. The Fossoil uses Blue.

balloons.head: Result
balloons.text: Both windows in the Light theme, with the Blue accent.

shots.title: Pumping gas
shots.caption: Filling a gas can at the pump, and the wagon's tank after refueling.

balloons.text: The card of the gas can in your hands. Unequip puts it away.
The action bar names the action: taking fuel, 34 percent.
The wagon's fuel gauge after refueling. The needle is near F.
Customers queue at the counter.
The watch you wear, at the left end of the belt.
The two hands: off hand (Secondary) and main hand (Primary). Both are empty here.
The buckle shows the profession. This one is for mechanics.
The action bar names the action and the item: smoking, a cigarette, 26 percent.
The full watch opens when you press the face of the small one. Drag it anywhere.
The small watch, at the left end of the belt.
The moodles are the game's own. Point at one for its name and description.
The thought bubble trails to its moodle. It also shows by itself when a moodle changes.

shots.title: Keeping count
shots.caption: Character window, Journal tab, with the Zombies killed section open.

balloons.text: Zombies killed, with the total at the right end of the heading.
Click the heading to show or hide the list.
Fire, vehicle and explosion kills have a colored square and count toward the total.
The other rows count kills by weapon type.

shots.title: Night shift
shots.caption: Dark theme with the blue accent, the dashboard at night, and the watch light.

balloons.text: Dark theme and blue accent, set from the window menu box.
At night the gauges glow amber. The HI lamp is lit.
LIGHT lights the watch's display.
The full watch tucks back onto the belt after a few seconds.

shots.title: Every window
shots.caption: The window menu and the help line are on every ZeD window.

balloons.text: The box at the right end of every title bar pulls down the window menu.
Theme, Accent, Text size, See-through and Controller highlight each open a list. Reset and ZeD setup are at the bottom of the menu.
Over a control, the line gives its help in plain words. Elsewhere it shows the window's own count.
With a controller it shows the buttons for what has focus.
Drag the grow box to resize. The bottom edge, the bottom corners and the sides work too.

shots.title: See-through
shots.caption: See-through runs from 100 to 60, and 90 is the default. Solid while in use makes the window under the pointer solid.

balloons.text: At 100 the window is solid.
At 60 the scene behind, here the lot and its cars, shows through the window.

shots.title: Controller highlight
shots.caption: Four ways to mark what the controller is on. Pick one in the window menu, under Controller highlight.

balloons.text: Pointing hand, the default: a hand at the left of the row.
Corner marks: four brackets round the row.
One wash: the whole row fills with the accent.
Marching ants: a dashed outline round the row.

shots.title: Hidden actions
shots.caption: Hidden actions: Folded (the default), Show all or Hide. Shown on Hair and beard, with no scissors or razor.

balloons.text: What you can't do yet folds into one row: "5 more with the right things".
Show all lists the same actions, greyed, each with what it needs.

shots.title: Inventory and loot
shots.caption: In ZeD, open containers sit side by side as columns. Drag an item to another column to move it.

balloons.text: Vanilla: an inventory window and a loot window. The buttons on the right edge pick a container.

balloons.head: Character window
balloons.text: The military backpack and the inventory, each in its own column.

balloons.head: World window
balloons.text: Each container in reach has its own column: the trunk, a duffel bag and the ground.

shots.title: List or grid
shots.caption: The Character window's inventory as a list and as a grid.

balloons.text: Press the list button for one row per item, with its category, condition and weight.
Press the grid button for a picture of each item, with its weight and condition.
Each picture carries the item's weight in its corner and its condition below.

shots.title: Item cards
shots.caption: Click an item to open its card. Cards also open for generators, campfires, farm plots, troughs, padlocks and liquids.

balloons.text: Marks: favorite, no-craft and dispose. Click a button to set one.
Kind, weight, hunger and thirst, then freshness with a square status mark.
Nutrition facts, set out like a food label. The card scrolls for the rest.
The X closes the card. The top row: the main action (Eat for food, Equip for a weapon) and More.
Condition, with a square status mark.
Combat facts: damage, range, swing, knockback and critical chance.

shots.title: Equipment tab
shots.caption: Drag a worn item to a bag or the ground to take it off.

balloons.text: The upper body on the left: head to hands, with small slots from the ears down to the rings.
The back and its bags, then the belt and below, on the right.
These buttons switch between list and doll.
A worn item. The bar under it is its condition.
An empty slot is drawn with a dashed outline.
The number is how many items are worn in that slot.
Vanilla: the Health tab.
The body figure. Hover a part to see its health and conditions.
Overall health: a framed bar and a percentage.
Pick an exercise. One that needs an item you do not carry is dimmed.
Set the minutes, 10 to 60.
This text says what the exercise trains.

shots.title: Thermal tab
shots.caption: Character window, Thermal tab, shown in three of its seven views.

balloons.text: The figure shows one reading for every body part, here the skin temperature.
One radio button for each view. The figure takes its colors from the view picked.
Core, air and wind temperatures sit under the figure.

shots.title: Context menus
shots.caption: Choose the strip or the list in Options, ZeD setup.

balloons.text: Vanilla: the right-click menu.
Strip: each action is an icon. The selected one is named above it.
A corner mark means the action opens a sub-menu.
List: one action to a row, with its icon. A > means a sub-menu.

shots.title: Action bar
shots.caption: Options, ZeD setup, Action bar: Verbose (words) or Simple (ten segments).

balloons.text: Vanilla: the progress bar.
ZeD: the action and the item in words, over the character.
The framed strip fills as the action runs.

shots.title: Crafting
shots.caption: World window, Crafting tab, with a recipe open.

balloons.text: Pick the station to craft at, and a category to look through.
Show: Ready lists only what you can make now. Press it for Known, then All.
Search by name, category or ingredient. Sort by Craftable, Known, Name, Freq or Recent.
A green square marks a recipe you can make now.
Craft stays dimmed while red squares show in the Required list.

shots.title: Building
shots.caption: World window, Building tab, with a recipe open.

balloons.text: Pick a category, or search the recipes by name.
Show: Ready is on, so the list holds only what you can build now. Nothing is ready yet.
Known: you have learned the recipe. 50s is how long it takes.
Required (0/7): everything the recipe needs. Red squares mark what is missing.
Build stays dimmed while red squares show in the Required list.

shots.title: Foraging and furniture
shots.caption: World window: the Foraging tab and the Furniture tab.

balloons.text: The tags give the zone's conditions, movement, season and weather.
The search radius in tiles, and the net change from modifiers.
Press Searching to start or stop looking. Crouch and Aim only show your stance.
The pop-up picks a category to look for. Finds are listed below, with distance, name and weight.
Five modes: Pick up, Place, Rotate, Disassemble and Repair. The lit one is in use.
Choose a mode, then point at furniture in the world.

shots.title: The belt
shots.caption: The hands sit at the left end of the belt, then the strap. A gun in the main hand adds a tab for its rounds.

balloons.text: The off hand is on the left and smaller, the main hand beside it. Each ring shows the item's condition.
Then the strap: four numbered slots, split evenly by the buckle.
One item in both hands: the main hand keeps its circle and ring, and the off hand peeks out from behind it.
A loaded gun shows its rounds on a tab out from under the main hand. 12+1 is twelve in the magazine and one chambered. One square per round.

shots.title: Speech, thoughts and hands
shots.caption: What your character says, and the action under way, over the head. The hands sit at the belt's left end, each with a condition ring.

balloons.text: What your character says shows in a balloon, in the theme's colours.
With the action bar on Verbose, the action shows in a thought bubble.
Off hand, then the larger main hand, at the belt's left end. Each ring is the item's condition.
One item in both hands: the main hand keeps its circle and the off hand peeks out from behind it.

shots.title: Moodles
shots.caption: The moodles are the game's own. ZeD places them where you choose and draws the note that explains one.

balloons.text: On the left edge, in the game's own column.
Or in a row above the belt, in the middle of the screen. ZeD draws this copy.
Or on the right edge, the game's own place for it.
Point at a moodle and a thought bubble names it and says what it means.

shots.title: Watches
shots.caption: The small watch on the belt shows the watch you wear, here in four models.

balloons.text: A watch worn on the left wrist sits left of the off hand, at the left end of the belt.
Press the face to open the full watch. Press it again to put it away.
The left pusher sets the game speed. The right one starts or pauses it.
Each model is drawn to match the watch you wear.
The main hand (Primary) sits right of the off hand (Secondary).

shots.title: Messages
shots.caption: Notes from other mods go into one window instead of covering the game. Questions still ask at once.

balloons.text: Each mod that sent something, with a count.
The mod's own Ok button works here.
A mod's notes can be shown as pop-ups again.
A strip names the mod for a few seconds. Click it to read.
The paper note on the belt opens Messages, with the count of new notes.

shots.title: The car radio
shots.caption: Each car's radio opens up close: tune it, store your stations, play a CD.

balloons.text: The display shows the band, the frequency, the station's name and the signal.
The left knob sets the volume. Push it to turn the radio on or off.
The right knob tunes the frequency.
Press a preset to listen. Hold one to store the tuned station.
SCAN steps through the stations until pressed again. SEEK goes to the next one. MUTE cuts the sound.
The play button starts and stops a CD. The eject button above MUTE gives it back.

shots.title: Dashboards
shots.caption: The key turns as the engine starts, the ash tray opens with a click, and the taxi's meter runs.

balloons.text: The taxi's meter: click the flag to start it, and again to stop it. Extra riders add to EXTRAS.
The hula girl sways in the turns.
The key turns OFF, ON and START while the engine cranks.
Ash trays open and shut with a click.

shots.title: Two-way radios
shots.caption: Walkie talkies, the ManPack and the ham sets each have their own face in the radio tab.

balloons.text: The button at the right of the header opens full view. A click on the face does too.
Every knob and key on the face works: volume, tuning, channels, memory and push to talk.
The red marker follows the frequency.
Range shows how far the set transmits.
Full view: the face on its own, with no window frame. Drag it anywhere.

shots.title: Ovens and microwaves
shots.caption: An oven or microwave shows its own controls in the Craft tab, and they can pop out into a window.

balloons.text: A button in the plate's corner pops the controls out into their own window.
The same controls work in the window. The line below shows on or off, and the heat.
The microwave has its own face: power level, time cook, number keys and start.

shots.title: Reading and writing
shots.caption: A newspaper opens in a reader, and a notebook opens as a page to write on.

balloons.text: The side column lists the stories. Pick one to jump to it.
Paper shows the page as printed. Words shows the same text in plain type.
Zoom the printed page with the buttons at the foot.
A page has a title, lines to write on and its page number.
The Pages list shows the first line of each page, or Blank.

shots.title: Fishing
shots.caption: While the line is out, the rod in your hands shows its tension above the belt.

balloons.text: The dial on the reel is the tension meter. Slack, its pointer rests low on the left.
The line sags while it is slack.
Tight: the rod bows, the pointer comes up and the wraps start to turn gold.
At the limit MAX lights red, the wraps run to red and the line goes pale red. Past it, the line snaps.

shots.title: Questions
shots.caption: The game's own questions and prompts, drawn as ZeD windows. The pad gets an on-screen keyboard.

crops.tag: A PROMPT AND THE PAD KEYBOARD

balloons.text: A question from the game. The answers sit in the band at the window's foot.
A prompt with a text box: Cancel and OK sit at the foot.
Hour and minute have minus and plus buttons, and a checkbox sets the alarm on.
On a controller the keyboard opens under the box. Its keys carry the pad's buttons.

shots.title: Controller
shots.caption: Every mouse action has a button: A is left click, X is right click, B backs out.

balloons.head: LT | RT
balloons.text: The game's own: aim and attack. On the map, zoom.

balloons.head: LB
balloons.text: Character window. No window open: LB + RB zooms out. Quick actions: LB + a button.

balloons.head: View
balloons.text: In a window: layout. No window open: hold for the ZeD wheel.

balloons.head: Menu
balloons.text: The game's pause menu.

balloons.head: RB
balloons.text: World window. No window open: RB + LB zooms in. Quick actions: RB + a button.

balloons.head: Y (Triangle)
balloons.text: Tap: open, hide or show both windows. Hold: close both.

balloons.head: B (Circle)
balloons.text: Back: close or back out.

balloons.head: A (Cross)
balloons.text: Left click: open, take, press.

balloons.head: D-pad
balloons.text: In a window: move from control to control. No window open: hold for a wheel (Character, World, Social, Here and now).

balloons.head: Left stick
balloons.text: Walk. Click it in a window to sort the list.

balloons.head: Right stick
balloons.text: Aim; both windows hide. Click it in a window: List or Grid. In a wheel: point.

balloons.head: X (Square)
balloons.text: Right click: the context menu.

shots.title: On a controller
shots.caption: Hold a D-pad direction for a wheel: Character, World, Social, Here and now. Point with the right stick, let go to take.

balloons.text: LB + A eats without opening the wheel. A slice on a chord shows it.
Under the pointer: the slice's name, its chord and what it does.
A slice that can't be done now says why.
The footer names what each button does here. The pictures are drawn for your controller.

shots.title: Quick actions
shots.caption: Hold LB or RB and press A, B, X, Y, L3 or R3: twelve actions from the wheels, set in ZeD setup or from a wheel.

balloons.text: Twelve chords: a bumper with a face button or a stick click.
A chooses the action. X clears it.
Put things back after an action. Off until you turn it on.
Every action on the wheels, in a list. The one on the chord you are editing is marked «.

shots.title: Themes and accents
shots.caption: Three base themes and nine accent colors, shown on the Character window. Each window can also have its own accent.

balloons.text: The accent color marks the open tab and the buttons that are on.
The title bar's right-hand box opens the window menu: Theme, Accent and more.

shots.title: Wallpapers
shots.caption: Desk, Settings menu: the picture on the monitor. A square marks the one in use.

balloons.text: Original wallpaper: the game's old title painting.
New wallpaper: the Build 42 title video plays on the monitor.
The main menu is a desk with a monitor. Each screen opens in a window on the monitor.
Desktop icons open the same screens as the menu.
There are a few things to find on the desk. Be careful emptying the trash.

shots.title: Options
shots.caption: ZeD setup comes first. The game's own pages follow, and say which settings ZeD replaces.

balloons.text: Theme, accent, text size, see-through and UI scale: radio buttons, swatches and sliders.
Game settings ZeD replaces are grayed out and say so.
Hidden actions is a pop-up menu: Folded, Show all or Hide.
Every setting is explained down here.

shots.title: Sandbox options in game
shots.caption: Change this save's sandbox settings from the pause window. Off until you turn it on in ZeD setup.

balloons.text: With Sandbox options in game turned on in ZeD setup, the pause window has a Sandbox options line.
The Changed and History pages list what you changed and let you put it back.
What it does, what changing it does to this save, and a tip.
Each setting says when a change takes effect: now, in new places only, or fixed.
Apply stays dim until something changes, and asks before it goes ahead.

shots.title: Mods
shots.caption: Mods: problems and conflicts, which copy the game uses, what each mod needs and what turning it off would do.

balloons.text: Tabs for problems, conflicts and the Workshop.
A mod in conflict says so in its row.
Each mod says what turning it off would do.
Choose file by file picks which mod's copy of a shared file runs.
Same file in two mods: the later mod's copy is the one used.
Same item in both: the game reads by file name, so order changes nothing.
A mod it needs that is not installed is marked.
A mod made for another game version says which.

shots.title: A mod's settings
shots.caption: A mod's own options, the sandbox settings it adds to each game, and Reset settings, which asks first.

balloons.text: The info pane's tabs: About, Options, Sandbox and Conflicts.
The mod's own options, kept as you change them. A square mark shows what you changed.
The settings files the mod keeps in Zomboid/Lua. Reset settings copies each, then empties it.
The sandbox settings it adds to each new game, read from the mod's own files, also while it is off.
Reset settings asks first: options back to their defaults, files emptied, copies kept in Zomboid/Lua/ZeD_reset.

shots.title: Picking files
shots.caption: Two mods with the same code file: pick whose copy the game runs, file by file. Single player only.

balloons.text: Every file both mods have, with the mod whose copy runs on each row.
Choose whose copy runs. A reload puts it in place, no restart.
Both copies side by side, with the lines that differ marked.
The band sums up the picks. Use these picks puts them in a helper mod, ZeD picks, which loads last.
The picks stay listed in the Conflicts tab, with Change picks and Undo picks.

shots.title: Turning a mod off
shots.caption: What turning a mod off does to a save: careful or not safe, and why. In a save's own list, a mod that is not safe asks first.

balloons.text: Saves keep their own mod lists, so the main list changes new games only.
Careful: the pane lists what the save would lose, reason by reason.
In a save's own list the pane speaks for that save: a map or tiles make it not safe, with the reasons.
A mod that is not safe asks first, in the band at the window's foot.

shots.title: Profiles and load order
shots.caption: A profile keeps a mod list with its load order. A row is marked when a mod loads before what it needs.

balloons.text: Loading a profile says what it turns off.
A mod it lists that you do not have is named, and stays off.
Each profile keeps its own load order.
Crafting Pack loads before the Crafting Core it needs.
Done waits until the order is fixed. Auto sets it.

shots.title: Uploading
shots.caption: Upload to the Workshop from one window. The description editor shows the page the way Steam will.

balloons.text: Who can see it, tags and the preview picture.
Build the page from blocks and whole sections.
Edit description opens the block editor.
The folder is checked before it goes up.
The page as Steam will show it.
A running count of characters: 698 of 7,950.
Anything that cannot be undone asks first.

shots.title: Loadouts (testers wanted)
shots.caption: New: save what you carry as a loadout, restock it before a trip, unpack it at home. Please test it and tell us in Bug reports.

balloons.text: Right-click what you carry: Save to loadout puts it on a named list.
The Loadouts fold, under the doll and the lists: the loadout, the days, and ready 1 of 5, the lines already on you.
Restock takes the rest from the building you are in, by the game's own actions.
The to-do: each supply and tool, how many you need and have, and where it goes.

shots.title: Radios and the CD player
shots.caption: The two radios, the hand-built radio and the CD player each have their own face in the radio tab.

balloons.text: POWER, VOL and TUNE work as on the set. A preset key held stores the station; pressed, it tunes back to it.
The Premium radio takes a disc you carry in its slot. EJECT gives it back.
The hand-built radio is the board you wired. The rocker turns it on.
Click the battery meter on the screen to change the battery.

shots.title: Television sets
shots.caption: The three television sets each have their own face. The screen shows the picture, snow or the off-air cards.

balloons.text: A tape plays on the screen: its title, then the lines it has shown.
Off the dial, or just after a channel change, the screen shows snow.
A station that is off the air shows its sign-off card, or the standby card once it has stopped for good.
The knob pulls on and pushes off, and turns for the volume. The dial has twelve stops.

shots.title: Washer and dryer
shots.caption: The washer, the dryer and the washer-dryer each have their own face. The game's own actions run them.

balloons.text: While it runs, the phase lamps step through wash, rinse and spin, and the drum turns.
The meter reads the water in the machine. FILL lights when a washer has none.
Power starts and stops it. It needs grid or generator power.
The door shows what is inside in the Loot pane.
WASH and DRY set the washer-dryer's mode.

shots.title: Machine plates
shots.caption: Ovens, microwaves and generators show their own controls, sized to fill the card at every UI scale.

balloons.text: BAKE, the number keys and START set and run the oven. The display shows the heat.
The microwave: power level, time cook, the number keys and start.
The engine switch starts and stops the generator. The gauge reads its fuel.
A warning shows when the generator stands indoors.
